page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a marginal note in the left margin beside the paragraph "Theoreticum est Ens". Running head at top with the page number at left. Catchword "Typus" at the lower right.

head.i: Cap.39. De principio primo, incomplexo, immediato, theoretico.

main_text.p: DIctæ sunt breviter principiorum affectiones; sequuntur eorundem species.
Principium est vel primum, vel ortum.
Principium primum est, quod commune est omnibus disciplinis.
Incomplexum est, quod consideratur extra dispositionem.
Estq; immediatum, vel mediatum: illud firmissimum, hoc minus firmum dicitur.
Immediatum est vel theoreticum, vel practicum & poëticum.

Principium primum immediatū & incomplexum in theoreticis.Theoreticum est Ens: cujus Synonyma ponimus Rem & Aliquid. Non enim facimus cum Arabibus, qui hæc tria, Ens, Rem, Aliquid, distinguunt. Antonius Andreas in 4. Metaph. cap. 3. q.5. diserte tradit, Ens esse principium simpliciter primum.
Ens est primus & ultimus omnium conceptuum: ut ostendunt erudite Keckerm. lib.1. Metaph. cap.1.& Timpl.Metaph.lib.1.cap.1.

page.notes: The initial D of "DIctæ" is a large woodcut-style initial, joined to the first word. "Itaq;" stands alone on its own line, set in italic with an ornament after it, and is given as its own paragraph. The line-break hyphen in "pra-cticum" and "pri-mum" is joined. The stray mark before "est" at the start of the line ("st" with a dot) is treated as printer's ornament, not a letter. No Greek or Hebrew on this page.
